'''Gisèle Massengo Mophou''' (also published as '''Gisèle Adélie Mophou Loudjom''') is a Cameroonian [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[numerical analysis|numerical analyst]] whose research involves [[control theory]] and [[fractional differential equation]]s.{{r|aas}} She is a professor at the [[University of the French Antilles]] in [[Pointe-à-Pitre]], [[Guadeloupe]], where she directs the Laboratoire de Mathématiques Informatique et Applications (LAMIA).{{r|lamia}}

==Education and career==
Mophou is originally from Cameroon.{{r|humboldt}} She earned a bachelor's degree in 1987, and a [[diplôme d'études approfondies]] in numerical analysis in 1997 at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in France. She completed her PhD in numerical analysis in 2000, at the University of the French Antilles.{{r|aas}}

She obtained a [[habilitation]] in 2010, and became a full professor at the University of the French Antilles in 2013.{{r|aas}} From 2017 to 2019 she returned to Cameroon, with the support of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], as German Research Chair at the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] Cameroon.{{r|humboldt}}

==Recognition==
Mophou was elected to the [[African Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.{{r|aas}}
